Question: If \(S\) is the set of points \(z\) in the complex plane such that \((3+4i)z\) is a real number, then \(S\) is a
Solution:
A complex number is real exactly when its imaginary part is zero. Write \(z=x+iy\), where \(x,y\) are real, so that \(z\) corresponds to the point \((x,y)\). Using \(i^2=-1\),
\[
(3+4i)(x+iy)
=(3x-4y)+i(4x+3y).
\]
Thus the product is real exactly when
\[
4x+3y=0,
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
 y=-\frac43x.
\]
This is the equation of a line through the origin. Every point on that line makes the imaginary part zero, and every admissible point satisfies this equation. The origin is included because a product equal to zero is real.

Therefore \(S\) is a \(\boxed{\text{line}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
